analysis.title: US inflation revives the October debate
key_insights: September US CPI came in above expectations for the second consecutive month, suggesting the summer easing in price pressures may have been temporary. Supercore inflation moderated, but renewed pressure in goods and housing cast doubt on the disinflationary trend.
Treasury yields surged and the dollar reached an 18-month high as markets revived expectations of another Fed rate hike.
Natixis still favours a Fed hold at the October meeting, but the decision has become a much closer call. It expects the Fed to wait for more data before reassessing in December.
Bowman and Williams have signalled there is no immediate need to tighten further, though the hot print gives hawkish FOMC members more ammunition.
ECB policymakers remain divided over further tightening. Lagarde has not yet seen second-round effects from higher energy prices, while Simkus said recent data could justify further tightening.
Escalating Middle East tensions pushed Brent above $106 intraday, reinforcing concerns about a prolonged energy shock.

US equities sold off broadly (S&P 500 -1.2%, Nasdaq -1.9%, Russell 2000 -2.0%) on rate-hike fears. Semiconductors (-3.6%) led declines, six of seven Mag-7 names closed lower, and the KBW Bank Index fell 2.9%.
European equities outperformed US peers, with the Stoxx 600 +0.4% at its highest close since September 29, led by health care and a strong ASML beat.
BAC Q3-2026 was a miss across the board: revenue +3% YoY to $30.0bn, expenses $19.7bn (+14%) including a $1.2bn regulatory settlement charge, net income $6.5bn (-17%), CET1 10.9% (-37 bps QoQ).
MS Q3-2026 was a revenue-driven beat on strong NII: revenue $20.3bn (+12% YoY), Equity Trading +41%, net income $4.9bn (+6%) above expectations, CET1 steady at 14.9%.
The October Beige Book showed moderate activity and rising price pressures in half of the districts, with consumers cautious, reinforcing expectations of a Fed pause this month.

market_movers.rationale: Q3-2026 missed across the board on softer revenues and a $1.2bn regulatory settlement charge. Adjusted net income was $8.1bn (+3%), which suggests the negative trend may reverse in Q4.
Q3-2026 was a revenue-driven beat on strong NII, with Equity Trading +41%. Net income of $4.9bn topped expectations.
A strong ASML beat helped lift European equities.
Orsted shares fell 4% after the US federal administration announced a review of the construction permit for the Revolution Wind offshore project.

earnings_insights: BAC Q3-2026 (reported): revenues $30.0bn, +3% YoY. Expenses $19.7bn (+14%) including a $1.2bn regulatory settlement charge for money laundering and sanctions violations. Net income $6.5bn reported (-17% YoY) and $8.1bn adjusted (+3%). Trading missed across the board, FICC down YoY, Equities +10%.

MS Q3-2026 (reported): revenues $20.3bn, +12% YoY. Operating charges $13.7bn (+12%). Net income $4.9bn (+6%), above expectations. Equity Trading +41%, FI Trading -8%, IB +2%, Wealth Management up 10% YoY to record revenues.
BAC CET1 ratio fell to 10.9% (-37 bps QoQ). AFS portfolio carries a -$5.2bn unrealized loss and the HTM portfolio a -$103.9bn unrealized loss.
ASML reported a strong beat, per the daily market recap. No figures were given.

tension_points.bull_case: Bowman and Williams say there is no immediate need to tighten. The Beige Book shows a cautious consumer and moderate activity, which supports a pause in October.
tension_points.bear_case: Core CPI beat for the second straight month (0.335% MoM versus 0.2% consensus) gives hawkish FOMC members ammunition. Markets revived expectations of another rate hike.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further hot inflation data before the December meeting would end the wait-and-see stance. Natixis names December as the point to reassess.
